Extract Draws From an Rvec

Source: R/extract_draws.R
extract_draws.Rd

Select a set of draws, specified using indices.

Usage

extract_draws(x, i)

Arguments

x

An rvec.

i

An index vector.

Value

An rvec with the same type, length, and element names as x, and length(i) draws. Selecting one draw still returns an rvec.

Details

Index i must be a numeric vector, consisting of whole numbers between 1 and n_draw(x). Duplicates are allowed. NAs are not. Draws are returned in the order specified by i.

See also

  • extract_draw() Extract one draw as an ordinary vector.

  • thin_draws() Randomly select draws without replacement.

  • n_draw() Number of draws.

Examples

x <- rvec(matrix(1:12, nrow = 4))
x
#> <rvec_int<3>[4]>
#> [1] 1,5,9  2,6,10 3,7,11 4,8,12
extract_draws(x, c(3, 1, 3))
#> <rvec_int<3>[4]>
#> [1] 9,1,9   10,2,10 11,3,11 12,4,12

## sample with replacement
set.seed(1)
i <- sample.int(n_draw(x), size = 10, replace = TRUE)
extract_draws(x, i)
#> <rvec_int<10>[4]>
#> [1] 5 (1, 9)  6 (2, 10) 7 (3, 11) 8 (4, 12)

## shared indices preserve alignment
y <- 2 * x
extract_draws(x, i)
#> <rvec_int<10>[4]>
#> [1] 5 (1, 9)  6 (2, 10) 7 (3, 11) 8 (4, 12)
extract_draws(y, i)
#> <rvec_dbl<10>[4]>
#> [1] 10 (2, 18) 12 (4, 20) 14 (6, 22) 16 (8, 24)
